Findings.title: Caller-supplied DeviceType string is interpolated into the RMAN script with only a non-empty check.
Findings.detail: DeviceType is a [string] with only [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]. It goes straight into the script text sent to RMAN. A value containing a semicolon or newline, such as 'DISK; DELETE NOPROMPT BACKUP;', ends the command and adds another. This command deletes data, so an injected command can destroy backups outside the ShouldProcess preview. REVIEW.md says a [string] in an RMAN script is a finding unless the attribute limits it to characters that cannot end or extend a command. Fix: use a [ValidateSet('DISK','SBT','SBT_TAPE')] or a strict pattern such as ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\z that is anchored with \z, and pin it with a test.

Findings.title: No test covers the new DeviceType parameter or its validation.
Findings.detail: The only test change updates the expected script for the default DISK value. Nothing passes a non-default DeviceType, checks that it reaches the script, or checks that a value containing a semicolon, newline or space is rejected. The S9 invariant now says DeviceType is validated, but its cited test only checks the default script. That test would still pass if the validation were removed, so the claim is unproven. The change also adds behaviour with no test that would fail without it.

Findings.title: The S9 invariant overstates the validation as a safety guarantee.
Findings.detail: S9 and the [SEC] comments describe the script as fixed text apart from a DeviceType that is 'validated non-empty'. Non-empty validation does not stop RMAN command injection. The wording presents an unsafe input as a validated one, and the entry carries no Limitation line. The invariant should state a real character restriction once the parameter has one.
